subject: MAP: Close plan & TTFT/streaming benchmarks for Medisquared
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Karen Liu <karen.liu@medisquared.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Close plan & TTFT/streaming benchmarks for Medisquared

Karen —

Following our call, attached is the initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with a focused performance-eval lane so procurement and engineering can align on acceptance criteria. High-level asks and proposed timelines below: 

- Goal: Validate streaming TTFT and live token latency at candidate model (rwd-llm-2B-fp16) to meet Medisquared UAT SLOs.
- Key metrics: TTFT (time-to-first-token) p50/p95/p99, streaming token latency p50/p95/p99, sustained throughput at concurrency (10, 50, 100) req/s.
- Test data: 250 production prompts (redacted examples) + 50 long-turn chats for streaming paths.
- Test environment: dedicated non-prod cluster (same region) with identical instance types; we need a test org and API key with quota.
- Acceptance criteria (suggested): TTFT p95 < 450ms; streaming p95 per-token < 120ms under 50 concurrent chats; <1% request errors.
- Timeline: baseline runs Wed 14-Apr; optimization iteration Thu 15-Apr; final results Fri 16-Apr.

Requested action from your side: confirm access (test org & sample prompts) and sign-off on the acceptance thresholds above. We’ll run the scripted benchmarking harness and share raw CSV + summaries. 

Attachments: medisquared_map_v1.pdf (MAP with responsibilities & dates).

Thanks — happy to tighten timelines if procurement is on a faster cadence.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP: Close plan & TTFT/streaming benchmarks for Medisquared

Rachel —

Thanks for the MAP. We can provide a test org and service account; procurement is reviewing the commercials but expects to be ready by EOW. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) For concurrency, are the listed targets (10/50/100) per-customer session or per-tenant? We plan to simulate per-customer sessions.
2) Do you need masked PHI in prompts for the long-turn chats, or are redacted examples sufficient?

If those are OK, we’ll send sample prompts and the test account by Tue morning.

—Karen
Karen Liu
VP Engineering | Medisquared

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Karen Liu <karen.liu@medisquared.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Close plan & TTFT/streaming benchmarks for Medisquared

Karen — thanks, that works. Quick answers and the testing matrix we’ll run: 

- Concurrency: simulate per-customer sessions (so concurrency = parallel active chat sessions). We’ll run the three levels against a mix of short prompts (avg 20 tokens) and long-turn chats (avg 250 tokens).
- PHI: redacted examples are fine for the latency work; if you want a PHI-preserving run later we can route via your private deployment.

Testing matrix (attached as part of MAP):
- Model: rwd-llm-2B-fp16 (primary), rwd-llm-1B-quant (fallback)
- Sequence lengths: short (20), medium (100), long (250) tokens
- Concurrency: 10 / 50 / 100 sessions
- Duration per run: 10 minutes sustained at target qps
- Metrics collected: TTFT per request, per-token streaming latency, throughput (tokens/s), error rates, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate.

We’ll upload raw CSVs to the shared folder (link below) and push summary plots. Can you confirm test org access by Tue 14:00 PDT? If so, we’ll run baseline Wed morning.

HubSpot (MAP record): https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/7592
Shared results doc: https://docs.redwood.com/s/medisquared/ttft-map

Thanks — attaching the MAP PDF again: medisquared_map_v1.pdf.

Rachel

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Karen Liu <karen.liu@medisquared.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 07:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Close plan & TTFT/streaming benchmarks for Medisquared

Quick engineering note on measurement and pass/fail so expectations are aligned before runs: 

- TTFT measurement: start = request arrival at edge; first token = first byte of stream returned to client. We’ll report wall-clock measurement and also trace spans for the datacenter path.
- Streaming per-token latency: measured at client-facing level per emitted token; reported as median and tail (p95/p99) per-run.
- Concurrency load profile: we’ll ramp to target QPS over 60s, sustain for 10min, then cool down.
- Acceptance criteria (final): 
  • TTFT p95 < 450ms
  • streaming per-token p95 < 120ms at 50 concurrent sessions
  • overall error rate < 1%

I’ll push the benchmark harness and the run config to the shared folder before the baseline. We’ll attach CSVs and a p95_latency_plot.png with the summary.

- Ben
Principal SWE, Inference Performance
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Karen Liu <karen.liu@medisquared.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Close plan & TTFT/streaming benchmarks for Medisquared — baseline results + next steps

Karen —

Attaching the baseline results from Wed’s run: benchmark_results_streaming.csv and p95_latency_plot.png. Highlights: 

- TTFT (rwd-llm-2B-fp16) — p50: 210ms; p95: 410ms; p99: 870ms (spike caused by a GC bump on the node during a 30s window).
- Streaming per-token latency (50 concurrent sessions) — p50: 18ms; p95: 110ms; p99: 320ms (long tail on token 1 of long-turn chats).
- Throughput: sustained 4.8k tokens/s aggregate at 50 concurrent sessions (measured across 5 nodes).
- Error rate: 0.4% (primarily transient timeouts while we tuned autoscaler).

Initial interpretation: we meet the suggested p95 TTFT < 450ms and streaming p95 < 120ms at 50 concurrents. The p99 tails warrant a short optimization pass (Ben’s team will try a kernel tweak and a cache warm-up script). We’ve added an item to the MAP for a 24-hour optimization window and a re-run Thursday morning.

Next asks from Medisquared to move toward procurement: 
- Confirm acceptance of the attached baseline (screenshot + CSV).
- If accepted, I’ll raise the SOW & procurement packet and loop in Finance.
